scope: Read-only audit of current WorldRenderer/RoomEngine source. The isolated harness compiles source into a unique /tmp output directory and measures private methods without GL; it is not an Android or Xiaomi FPS test.

interaction_work.source_behavior: updateInteraction runs after render every frame. When best target is non-null, it serializes the unchanged descriptor and constructs a new JSONObject each frame. The UI interaction poll/getInteraction deep-copies at about 10 Hz.

state_update_behavior.evidence: RoomEngine.applyPendingState returns when pendingStateJson equals appliedStateJson; otherwise WorldRenderer.applyState is called. updateNavigation is called from applyState, so navigation map/descriptor updates occur only for changed state.

assessment: Movement collision is skipped entirely when both input axes are zero. Movement plus look at the sampled doorway contact measured about 7.3–7.7 microseconds per call on the host; direct floorY/collides queries at spawn measured about 7.2–18.4 microseconds.

A stable interaction hit causes repeat JSON allocation (about 3.6–4.0 KiB per rendered frame on this host); retaining an immutable snapshot until best target or descriptor revision changes is a semantics-preserving candidate.

The measured host hot paths are orders of magnitude below a 100ms frame and do not explain 10 FPS by themselves. Android ART, rendering, EGL/Surface composition, thermal limits, and device-specific GPU costs were not measured.

Exact-safe collision optimization candidates are primitive slab math in rayBox, precomputed triangle AABBs/floor-plane data, or a conservative per-triangle spatial index that returns the same candidate set. Preserve all triangles and current collision predicates.
